title: System evaluation snapshot
description: One dimension-level evaluation of the Editorial Learning Core itself (AES-V2.14 / SUE-573), distinct from any article/artifact quality record. Judges whether V2 is getting better or merely bigger, never with one aggregate number. Both evals/system/current.json (kind: current, a derived index over the newest snapshot) and every file under evals/system/snapshots/ (kind: snapshot) conform to this schema. See evals/system/README.md for the evaluation contract and docs/architecture/V2-EDITORIAL-LEARNING-CORE.md §11 for the spine this implements. Deliberately carries no field capable of expressing an aggregate/overall score — scripts/lib/system-eval-core.mjs additionally rejects any disallowed score-shaped key found anywhere in the document, since additionalProperties:false alone cannot forbid a badly-named string value.

snapshot_id.description: Stable id. A real snapshot lives on disk at evals/system/snapshots/<slug-after-system-eval:>.json. The single current.json instance always carries the sentinel id system-eval:current.

kind.description: snapshot: one immutable, dated evaluation under snapshots/. current: the derived, rebuildable summary at current.json — always identical to the newest snapshot's judgement, never hand-edited independently of one.

derived_from_snapshot.description: Required non-null when kind is current: the snapshot_id current.json was rebuilt from. Required null when kind is snapshot: a snapshot is authored directly, never derived.

evaluation_trigger.description: Why this evaluation ran. The scorecard never runs after every article or asset (docs/architecture/V2-EDITORIAL-LEARNING-CORE.md §11) — only on one of these declared triggers.

trigger_note.description: One or two sentences on the concrete circumstance behind evaluation_trigger — never left to be inferred later from a date alone.

dimensions.description: Exactly the ten SUE-573 dimensions, each appearing exactly once. scripts/lib/system-eval-core.mjs enforces the count and the fixed id set — this schema's item shape cannot by itself (no minItems/uniqueItems in this repo's JSON-Schema subset).

known_gaps.description: Evidence gaps recorded honestly instead of papered over with an invented field or store. At minimum the two gaps named in evals/system/README.md (no revision/replan lineage; no cost/context proxy) must appear somewhere across the surface's known_gaps.

activation.description: The SUE-573 activation/sufficiency judgement: not a rigid quota, a declared and revisable read of whether repeated patterns can yet be distinguished from one-off incidents.

asks.description: The question this dimension answers, in one sentence.

evidence_sources.description: The static, load-bearing declaration: which real repository paths and record fields this dimension is ever allowed to read from. Each entry is `<repo-relative-path>[#<field-or-key>][ — <note>]`; scripts/lib/system-eval-core.mjs resolves the path (and, when present, checks the field/key text actually appears in that path) rather than trusting the string. A dimension with no real evidence source yet must say so here and in insufficient_evidence_when — never invent a field or a file to look measurable.

insufficient_evidence_when.description: What makes INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE the honest answer for this dimension right now (or in general, structurally).

evidence_refs.description: The actual evidence this specific judgement rests on, drawn only from evidence_sources above. Every non-INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE state requires at least one entry here (scripts/lib/system-eval-core.mjs rejects a HEALTHY/WATCH/STRUCTURAL_RISK claim with none). Each entry uses the same `path[#field][ — note]` convention as evidence_sources and must resolve to a real path.

interpretation.description: What the evidence actually shows, in plain language a reviewer with no chat history can check against the cited refs.

judgement_rules.description: What distinguishes each state for this dimension. Quantitative signals may be named here, but the rule is always a judgement a human or reviewer applies, never a formula that outputs a score.

owner_contract.description: Which existing or planned contract should own filling this gap. This package identifies gaps; it does not resolve them by adding fields of its own.
